messages:
maria: noticed a canary regression: a single safetensors fragment signature failure caused the streaming loader to abort and fall back to a full synchronous load, doubling p95 for some requests
jon: thanks. which verification step failed? sha256 or signature?
maria: sha256 matched, signature verify failed. loader then aborted the streaming path and hit legacy rehydrate sync path
kevin: that matches a theory i had about global aborts on per-fragment failures. we currently treat any fragment verify error as fatal
tia: for private deploys we also rotate keys often; could be key mismatch rather than corruption
jon: throwing out an approach: per-fragment fallthrough instead of global abort. options: retry from source (cache-bypass), re-request signature, or mark fragment degraded and continue streaming others
maria: sketched manifest additions: add fragment metadata `fallthrough_policy` with values: "reject", "retry-source", "degrade-stream" and optional `signature_key_id` to speed key lookup
kevin: good. default should be strict: v1 manifests have implicit `reject`. v2 manifests can opt into looser behavior
jon: loader flow proposal:
- verify sha256 first
- if sha mismatch -> reject immediately
- if sha ok but sig fails -> consult fragment.fallthrough_policy
  - "retry-source": re-fetch with cache-bypass header once, then reverify
  - "degrade-stream": accept only if sha matches and manifest has `allow_degraded_sha=true`, mark fragment as degraded and emit telemetry
  - "reject": abort top-level load and surface model-load-failure
maria: rationale: sha matching gives bit-level integrity; signature ensures provenance. degrade only when customer explicitly opts in to avoid silent tamper acceptance
tia: we should add `public_key_id` at model level too so runtime can select keys without KMS roundtrips per fragment
kevin: telemetry to add: fragment_sig_fail_count, fragment_fallback_type, fallback_retries, model_load_latency_impact histogram
maria: add feature flag `runtime.flags.fragment_fallback=canary|all` so we can roll this on canary before wider rollout
jon: tests matrix:
- sha ok + sig fail + retry-source -> succeed after re-fetch
- sha ok + sig fail + degrade_stream with allow_degraded_sha=false -> reject
- sha mismatch -> reject
- key rotation: signature_key_id picks rotated key
- network flake: ensure retry doesn't thundering-herd
kevin: compatibility: loader recognizes manifest version header. unknown fields ignored. v1 behavior preserved (reject). docs needed for model publishers to include new fields
maria: ops note: private deployments default to `reject` and surface clear errors. public hosted canary can opt into degrade for non-critical models
tia: who takes RFC/patch?
kevin: i'll draft a short RFC + prototype loader changes. target PR next week
maria: i'll wire metrics and a canary job to exercise edge cases
jon: i'll build the test harness and add unit/integration tests
maria: also update publisher onboarding docs to mention `signature_key_id` and `fallthrough_policy`
kevin: filing RFC and will link here when ready :thumbsup:
warmup-bot: scheduled canary run 2026-03-22T09:00Z - will post results
maria: thanks everyone, this should keep p95 from spiking during transient signature/key issues
